claims.text: Substrate preheating at 350–450°C combined with adaptive laser-power modulation during L-PBF will reduce residual thermal stresses in miniature AlCrFeNiSi components.
The combined intervention will improve the mechanical properties of miniature AlCrFeNiSi components relative to conventional high-thermal-load processing.
The feedstock is AlCrFeNiSi powder in its as-supplied morphology, composition, and particle-size distribution.
The build platform will be maintained at 350–450°C during printing.
Adaptive laser-power modulation will optimize energy input for miniature geometries.
A build-platform temperature of 350–450°C is an applicable processing window for miniature AlCrFeNiSi components made by L-PBF.
The L-PBF process will use a controlled atmosphere and adjusted laser energy density, with post-build assessment at room temperature.
The intervention will reduce thermal gradients between deposited layers.
Reduced thermal gradients will limit rapid cooling and microstructural inhomogeneity.
Lower or better-controlled energy input can reduce crack formation during L-PBF.
Preheating decreases the temperature differential between the melt pool and substrate, thereby reducing thermal shock and stress.
Adaptive laser-power modulation produces a more uniform energy distribution.
More uniform energy distribution facilitates controlled solidification and a refined microstructure.
Intervention-treated components will have lower XRD-measured residual stress than room-temperature-platform, constant-high-power controls.
Intervention-treated components will have higher tensile strength and ductility than controls.
The combined preheating and adaptive-power approach will provide a simpler processing regime than conventional high-thermal-load processing.
The baseline consists of L-PBF on a room-temperature platform using constant high laser power.
The hypothesis is limited to miniature AlCrFeNiSi L-PBF components and may not transfer to larger builds or other alloys.
The optimal preheating temperature and adaptive laser-power parameters depend on powder characteristics and thermal behavior and remain undetermined.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant residual-stress reduction exceeding 10% together with improved tensile strength and ductility will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention adds both active platform-temperature control and adaptive laser-power modulation, yet the predicted outcome calls the resulting regime simpler without defining a complexity metric or explaining how the added controls simplify processing.
